To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of aggressive behaviors increases 5-HT neuron activity and that preventing such increase in activity reduces the expression of such behaviors.
the performance of aggressive behaviors increases the activity of 5-HT cells in the dorsal raphe.
activation of serotonergic transmission increases during performance of aggressive behaviour in rats, and that this activation is necessary for the expression of aggressive behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of serotonin in aggressive behavior, and we are particularly interested in the role of the serotonin 5-HT1B receptor subtype in the control of aggressive behavior.
the role of the serotonin system in aggressive behavior and its modulation by environmental and pharmacological factors.
the neurobiology of aggression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
serotonergic activity during aggressive behavior is not necessarily low but is increased.
the activation of serotonergic neurons is required for expression of aggressive behavior.
high-aggressive rats have a higher level of serotonergic activity during the performance of aggression than low-aggressive rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation of 2 serotonin receptors, 5-HT(1A) and 5-HT(7), is required for the initiation and maintenance of aggressive behavior, whereas the activation of the serotonin transporter is required for the inhibition of aggressive behavior.
5-HT neurotransmission is not only involved in the expression of aggressive behavior, but also in the control of the expression of aggressive behaviors.

high-aggressive rats are characterized by low 5-HT neurotransmission in basal conditions, but that during performance of aggression, 5-HT activity is increased, and that this increase is necessary to maintain high-aggressive behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-HT neurotransmission is increased during the performance of aggression.
the activation of  5-HT neurons is necessary for the expression of aggressive behavior.
5-HT activity is increased, not decreased, during the performance of aggression.
